close_reason: Decision-type finding: ratifies preservation of the 'hand-built RFC 5322 byte literals — never derived from the code under test' doc-comment at crate-jmap-mime/benches/mime_pipeline.rs:20-22. The comment is already in place. No code change required; finding documents the design choice for future contributors.
description:
Why this choice is correct: the bench fixtures in crate-jmap-mime/benches/mime_pipeline.rs are hand-built &str / Vec<u8> RFC 5322 byte literals (build_small_plain, build_medium_multipart, build_large_deep_multipart). They are NOT generated by calling mime-tree's own parse/serialize round-trip, or by re-using crate-internal helper structs to construct the byte stream.

This matches the workspace test-integrity rule: 'tests must use independent fixtures (hand-written JSON from RFC examples, or OpenSSL/pyca output). Never derive expected values from the code under test.' For a benchmark, the equivalent rule applies — a bench whose fixture is generated by the code under test cannot detect a regression that changes both the fixture and the parse output in the same direction.

A future contributor might suggest 'simplifying' by replacing build_medium_multipart with a one-liner that constructs a ParsedMessage in memory and re-serializes it. That suggestion should be rejected. The whole bench design depends on the input being a stable RFC 5322 byte sequence the parser has never seen before.

The decision is documented in the file-level doc comment at lines 21-22: 'All fixtures are hand-built RFC 5322 byte literals — never derived from the code under test.' Preserve this comment under refactor.
title: Bench fixtures are hand-built RFC 5322 bytes, never derived from code under test
